newsitem.title: BELGIUM: PetroFina sees 1996 profit up 38 percent.
newsitem.headline: PetroFina sees 1996 profit up 38 percent.

text.p: Belgian oil and gas group PetroFina SA said on Tuesday full-year 1996 net profit should rise to 16.0 billion Belgian francs from 11.6 billion in 1995.
Including minority interests, consolidated net profit would be around 16.7 billion francs, up from 12.3 billion last year, a spokeswoman for the company told Reuters.
Cash flow was estimated at 45 billion Belgian francs, or 1,935 francs a share, compared with 39 billion francs, or 1,691 francs a share.
Final group profit figures are due to be released in March.
In a statement, PetroFina provided the following breakdown of its results (in billions of Belgian francs):
The company said profit rose mainly due to higher crude oil prices and higher U.S. gas prices and an improvement in refining and marketing operations.

PetroFina said upstream oil and gas production was flat compared with 1995 at 85.6 million barrels of oil equivalent compared with 85.3 million barrels. Oil production fell 1.5 percent to 50.5 million barrels while gas output rose 4.0 percent to 210 billion cubic feet.
Chemicals results were hit however by lower margins.

PetroFina said it planned to invest 37 billion Belgian francs in 1997, up from 34 billion francs in 1996. Upstream, the investment would focus on the North Sea Ekofisk and Armada projects and on Tempa Rossa in Italy. In chemicals, PetroFina said it hoped to increase high density polyethylene production in the U.S.
